title: Roles, Responsibilities & Shared Goals
summary: Learn how clear roles, responsibilities, boundaries, and shared goals help teams coordinate work without confusion or duplicated effort.
objectives: Explain the difference between a team role, responsibility, and shared goal.
Identify problems caused by unclear ownership or overlapping responsibilities.
Recognize when to act independently and when to coordinate with others.

vocab.def: The function or position a person holds within a team or work process.
A task, duty, decision, or result a person is expected to handle.
Clear responsibility for making sure an assigned action or outcome is addressed.
A result that multiple people contribute toward together.

sections.heading: Roles help organize teamwork
sections.body: Teams function more effectively when people understand who is responsible for which parts of the work. Roles help organize responsibility, communication, decision making, and accountability.

sections.heading: Shared goals connect different responsibilities
sections.body: People on the same team may perform very different tasks. Their work becomes connected when those tasks contribute to the same larger result.

sections.heading: Unclear ownership creates risk
sections.body: When nobody knows who owns a task, work can be duplicated, delayed, forgotten, or completed incorrectly. Clear ownership does not mean one person works alone; it means responsibility is visible.

sections.heading: Know your boundaries
sections.body: Teamwork does not require doing work outside your role, training, authority, or safety limits. Strong team members know when to act and when to coordinate, ask, escalate, or hand work to someone else.

practice.prompt: Two team members both assume the other person is responsible for submitting an important document. What teamwork problem is present?
practice.answer: Ownership is unclear. The team should identify who is responsible and confirm the expected action and deadline.

practice.prompt: A task affects your team but is outside your authority. What should you do?
practice.answer: Coordinate with or escalate to the person or role that has the proper authority.

quiz.question: Why is clear ownership important in teamwork?
options: It makes responsibility visible and reduces gaps or duplicated work
It means one person must complete the entire project alone
It eliminates the need for communication
It allows people to ignore work outside their own task
quiz.answer: It makes responsibility visible and reduces gaps or duplicated work

lab.objective: Create a simple team responsibility map showing the shared goal, roles, task ownership, boundaries, and points where coordination is required.
